method: Two rounds. Round 1 (10-photo run) surfaced a real design flaw: the named-text cross-check compared alt_text against a photo's stored visible_text with no stoplist, and a read-only frequency query against production photo_metadata.visible_text (22,442 rows, 11,512 distinct values) showed the highest-frequency values are generic vocabulary alt_text is expected to use — volleyball 1,025x, home 320x, team 220x, blue 88x, court 48x, ball 76x, dive 44x — meaning the unfiltered check would have hard-failed ingest on a large fraction of real photos over words that identify nobody. Added a stoplist (NAMED_TEXT_STOPWORDS) grounded in that measured distribution; a genuinely identifying single word (a school/team name, a surname) and any multi-word entry are unaffected. Round 2: re-ran the real, fixed extractOne against the same 10 DWdCET (Milliken at North Central) photos used for the captions receipt, this time capturing each photo's own visible_text and running inspectAltText against it — 10/10 alt-text-contract clean, including on rows whose visible_text was CARDINALS/MILLIKIN/PEPSI/GENEVA/NORTH-CENTRAL/VOLLEYBALL/SPORTS (real identifying and generic values coexisting; none produced a false reject or missed a real one, since none of the identifying values appeared in any alt_text). Read all 10 source images directly and checked each alt_text against the frame: 10/10 correctly avoid every jersey number, name, and piece of printed text. 3 of 10 (DSC09432, 09435, 09437) mislabel the on-court action verb (serve vs. set vs. spike) — a pre-existing vision-model action-classification limitation shared with the caption on the same photos, not specific to alt_text and not fixed here. Also found and fixed, this session: scripts/ingest-album.ts's photo_metadata upsert never wrote alt_text at all (extractOne returned it, nothing persisted it) — confirmed by reading the upsert payload; now included.
scope: production visible_text frequency query (22,442 rows), stoplist fix grounded in it
